content: Tecovirimat is a weak inducer of the enzyme CYP3A4. When co-administered with medications that are sensitive substrates of CYP3A4, it is important to monitor these drugs for potential reductions in their effectiveness. Tecovirimat can decrease the levels or effects of several drugs, including naloxegol, naldemedine, nefazodone, netupitant/palonosetron, nevirapine, nicardipine, nifedipine, nilotinib, nimodipine, nisoldipine, norethindrone (including its acetate and transdermal forms), olaparib, ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir & dasabuvir, ondansetron, osimertinib, ospemifene, oxycodone, paclitaxel (including protein-bound forms), palbociclib, panobinostat, paricalcitol, pazopanib, perampanel, pomalidomide, ponatinib, praziquantel, primaquine, progesterone (micronized and natural forms), quazepam, quetiapine, quinidine, quinine, ranolazine, regorafenib, ruxolitinib (including topical forms), salmeterol, saxagliptin, sildenafil, simvastatin, sirolimus, solifenacin, sonidegib, sorafenib, sufentanil, sunitinib, suvorexant, tacrolimus, tadalafil, tamsulosin, tasimelteon, tazemetostat, temsirolimus, teniposide, tetracycline, tezacaftor, theophylline, tiagabine, ticagrelor, ticlopidine, tinidazole, tipranavir, and tofacitinib. This reduction in drug levels or effects occurs due to the impact of tecovirimat on hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, tecovirimat is a weak inhibitor of the enzymes CYP2C8 and CYP2C19. It can increase the levels or effects of drugs metabolized by these enzymes, such as nelfinavir, paclitaxel, pantoprazole, pentamidine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, pioglitazone, progesterone (micronized), rabeprazole, repaglinide, riociguat, rosiglitazone, sertraline, and tofacitinib. Monitoring for adverse effects is recommended when tecovirimat is co-administered with sensitive substrates of CYP2C8 or CYP2C19. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. In the context of live smallpox and mpox (vaccinia) vaccines, animal studies suggest that co-administration with tecovirimat may reduce the immune response to the vaccine. However, the clinical impact of this interaction on vaccine efficacy in humans remains unknown, as no human studies have been conducted. For all these interactions, it is crucial to use caution and closely monitor the effectiveness and safety of the affected medications.
